body.heading: Pairs of opposites
paragraphs: Opposites are word pairs that face away from each other: hot and cold, up and down, rough and smooth. Your home is full of them, hiding in plain sight.
Write some opposite pairs on your paper: big and small, soft and hard, light and dark, fast and slow. Leave space to write what you find.

body.heading: Hunt the pairs
paragraphs: Find something big, then find its opposite — something small. A big spoon and a tiny spoon make a perfect pair.
Touch is allowed for rough and smooth. Sound works for loud and quiet — a tap on a pot is loud, a tap on a cushion is quiet.

body.heading: Tricky opposites
paragraphs: Some opposites hide. Where is something empty next to something full? Something new next to something old?
When your list is full, read it aloud like a poem of pairs. Opposites help words — and brains — stay organised.

takeaway: Opposites come in pairs, and hunting them at home sharpens your words and your noticing.
safetyNotes: Only handle objects an adult says are safe. Test loud things gently — no banging near ears.
screenFreeExtension: Play opposites with your body — stretch tall, curl small, move fast, move slow.
